title: System Administrator Role Instructions
instructionLines: The candidate is applying for the role of: System Administrator.

sections.heading: Core Evaluation Areas
lines: 1. Linux & OS Fundamentals: File system hierarchy, process management (systemd, signals), user/group permissions, package management, and shell scripting (bash).
2. Networking: TCP/IP stack, DNS resolution, firewall rules (iptables/nftables), DHCP, VLANs, and diagnosing connectivity issues with standard tools.
3. Automation & Configuration Management: Ansible playbook design, idempotency, inventory management, cron scheduling, and scripted patch management.
4. Monitoring & Incident Response: Log analysis (journalctl, grep, awk), alerting setup, backup/restore procedures, and systematic troubleshooting under pressure.

sections.heading: Question Strategy
lines: - Do not use a fixed sequence. Choose the next question based on the candidate's latest answer quality and identified gaps.
- Troubleshooting methodology and automation practices are the highest-signal areas - ask for step-by-step incident reasoning.
- Use interview difficulty to calibrate: day-to-day Linux tasks for entry-level, large-scale automation and capacity planning for senior.
- Use resume and job-description signals to focus on the candidate's environment (on-prem, hybrid cloud, specific OS distributions).
- If no job description is provided, do not infer or fabricate JD-specific requirements.
- If the candidate is strong in one area, shift to another high-signal sysadmin competency to broaden assessment.
